text:
[RFCS.10.5] A replaying reader ([LFST.9.6]) MUST apply each `ClockAdvance` by
advancing the replay engine's monotonic clock to `clock_ns` and setting its
wall clock to `wall_ns` before processing the next atom. When `has_wall` is
false the recorded wall clock had no value: the reader leaves the replay
engine's wall clock without one and ignores `wall_ns`, so a `now()` the
recording faulted ([LTIM.2.8.3]) faults again in the replay.

The reader **must** end the replay with `DS_ERR_TIME_RANGE` at a `ClockAdvance`
whose `clock_ns` is outside the monotonic clock's range ([LTIM.2.8.2]), as a
host's move past the range is refused ([NTST.3.1]).

---

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__replay_run_holds_what_was_held
idris.note: Applying each `ClockAdvance` before the next atom is what makes the replay engine end where the recording engine ended, from any starting clocks.

idris.name: rfcs_10_5__replay_drives_the_engine
idris.note: The reader's rule at the composed pump: a tick history replays to the recording's final state.

idris.name: rfcs_10_5__replay_run
idris.note: THE REPLAYING READER: each `ClockAdvance` sets both clocks before the next atom is processed, as the clause requires; generic in what an input does.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__replay_holds_what_was_held
idris.note: Applying each `ClockAdvance` to both clocks before the next atom, as the clause requires, is what makes the replay hold the recording's samples from any starting clocks.

idris.name: rfcs_10_5__clock_atom_goes_first
idris.note: THE CLOCK ATOM GOES FIRST. Written input-first, every sample is on the trace and the replay still holds the wrong one: each input is consumed under the clocks of the step before it. What a conforming recorder must do, by the one that does not.

idris.name: rfcs_10_5__record_input_first
idris.note: A recorder that writes a step's input BEFORE the step's `ClockAdvance`: the shape [LTIM.2.8.5] forbids ('must record a sample before it records the input or the pump boundary the sample was taken for'). The clause binds the replayer to apply a `ClockAdvance` before the atom after it, which is why the order matters. The refused shape.

idris.name: rfcs_10_5__replay
idris.note: THE REPLAY: the samples a replay engine holds, one per input it consumes. It has the atoms and its own clocks and nothing else; a `ClockAdvance` sets both clocks before the next atom, as the clause requires, and an input is consumed under the clocks as they then stand.
